DETECTOR_REFUTED.what_broke: the anchor resolver takes the FIRST Windows path in a candidate record. For 58 of 161 candidates that path is a SHARED PROGRAM DOC (08-WORKFLOW-ARCHAEOLOGY..., 08-WORKFLOW-CANDIDATE-REGISTRY.json, main-mirror.git), not the candidate's own body.
DETECTOR_REFUTED.self_contradiction_tell: 32 distinct candidate ids 'resolved' to ONE file. 32 distinct candidates cannot all BE one file, so the probe disagreed with itself and its duplicate verdicts are void.
DETECTOR_REFUTED.consequence: the 5 byte-identical groups are resolver artifacts. They are NOT 5 duplicate-candidate findings and must not be reported as such.
DETECTOR_REFUTED.what_survives: the 3 same-name pairs, which resolved to genuine distinct bodies and are all MATERIALLY-DISTINCT (agent-as-judge: 11,959 B agent .md vs 16,045 B SKILL.md, not byte-identical; codex: 6,128 B agent .md vs 11,227 B plugin README, not byte-identical; ralph-loop: 6,054 B plugin README vs 1,967 B vault SKILL.md, not byte-identical, max similarity 0.0293)

methodology_defect_found_and_fixed_in_th.what: my first pass called councilspec.semantics.errors(spec). errors() FILTERS Finding objects; it does not take a spec. Iterating the dict yielded strings and raised "'str' object has no attribute 'severity'" on 100% of inputs.
methodology_defect_found_and_fixed_in_th.consequence_if_unnoticed: it would have reported 0/48 protocols and 0/69 presets validating - a fabricated total failure
methodology_defect_found_and_fixed_in_th.how_it_was_caught: the fire rate was 100% including the 6 known-VALID example files; a detector that fires on every input including known-good is a detector failure, not a finding
methodology_defect_found_and_fixed_in_th.fix: errors(check(spec)); re-run gives 48/48 and 69/69 with 6/6 known-valid passing and 10/10 known-invalid firing

findings_beyond_the_floors.nuance: receipt.schema.json IS the one basename that exists anywhere - at platform/schema/receipt.schema.json (36,926 bytes, compiles 2020-12, usable standalone). So Wave 1 DID build the receipt schema, but at a path no work unit references. The remaining 268 paths (research-claim-record, council-design-note, test-receipt, measurement-run, conformance-report, audit-finding, foundry-artifact, ...) have no file anywhere in the repo.
findings_beyond_the_floors.why_it_matters: predicate condition 4 is 'artifact parses against its schema'. With the schema path unresolvable for every unit, condition 4 cannot be satisfied by any unit as catalogued - either the catalog paths must be remapped to platform/schema/, or 269 schemas must be authored there.

findings_beyond_the_floors.claim: The registry floor clears by exactly ONE candidate (161 vs 160), and two of the three counting decisions that produce 161 are discretionary.
findings_beyond_the_floors.evidence: count_sensitivity_table: 164 raw elements -> 163 after excluding the WFA3-MANIFEST row -> 161 after excluding WFA3-074-REJECT and WFA3-082-REJECT
findings_beyond_the_floors.why_it_matters: if either REJECT row is later ruled countable the floor is comfortably met (163); if either currently-counted candidate is later ruled a fork or a duplicate, the floor is MISSED. There is no headroom. A single reclassification flips the verdict.
findings_beyond_the_floors.recommendation: add candidates, or record an explicit counting rule in the registry so the 161 is not re-litigated

findings_beyond_the_floors.claim: A name-only fork filter drops the registry to 158, BELOW the 160 floor. All 3 collisions were individually falsified as forks, so 161 stands - but the margin means the choice of normalisation rule is load-bearing for the verdict.
findings_beyond_the_floors.evidence: 3 collision groups (agent-as-judge, codex, ralph-loop); name+provenance key produces 0 collisions; ralph-loop settled by direct measurement (plugin ships no SKILL.md, max similarity 0.0293)
findings_beyond_the_floors.residual_UNVERIFIED: the agent-as-judge and codex pairs were falsified from artifact TYPE and UPSTREAM divergence, not yet from a body-level byte comparison. The renamed-copy sweep in _wave1_fork_probe.py settles it; it was still running when this artifact was written.

findings_beyond_the_floors.settling_action: rule explicitly whether a marketplace shell counts; if it does not, 3+ new candidates are needed to clear 160

findings_beyond_the_floors.claim: My first body-level duplicate sweep reported 5 byte-identical candidate groups, the largest with 32 members. That was a DETECTOR FAILURE in my own probe, not a finding: the anchor resolver returned a shared PROGRAM DOC for 58 of 161 candidates.
findings_beyond_the_floors.tell: 32 distinct candidate ids cannot all be one file. A probe whose output contradicts itself is a broken instrument.
findings_beyond_the_floors.why_recorded: so the number 5 is not later cited as 5 duplicate candidates. Recording the refuted wording rather than deleting it.
findings_beyond_the_floors.what_a_correct_body_sweep_needs: a per-candidate BODY field (the artifact's own path), not a first-path-in-the-record heuristic. 21 of 161 candidates have no readable anchor at all, so even a fixed resolver would cap at 140/161 = 87% coverage.

findings_beyond_the_floors.claim: The protocols floor is met with margin ZERO (48 of 48). Any single protocol file being retired, renamed off the *.councilspec.json glob, or failing validation drops the floor.

findings_beyond_the_floors.claim: work-unit.normative.schema.json and work-unit.strict.schema.json compile but cannot be instantiated standalone; they chain by absolute $id and need a referencing.Registry holding the sibling schemas.
findings_beyond_the_floors.why_it_matters: any consumer that does jsonschema.validate(instance, json.load(open(strict_schema))) will raise Unresolvable at runtime, not at load. This is a usage contract that needs documenting, not a broken schema.

findings_beyond_the_floors.claim: Validating council files with JSON Schema alone would miss half the defect classes the project's own negative corpus defines.
findings_beyond_the_floors.evidence: 5 of 10 shipped invalid examples pass JSON Schema and are caught only by councilspec/semantics.py (count-min>max, source-expression drift, delegation cycle, round-cap incoherence, idea-gate-without-brainstorm)
findings_beyond_the_floors.why_it_matters: any downstream gate that validates presets/protocols must run BOTH layers. A schema-only gate is a fail-open gate.
